title: Sexual dimorphism of the face and skull

queue.claim: Default sex-specific young-adult norms used as fitting priors: n–gn 121.3 ± 6.8 (M) / 111.8 ± 5.2 (F) mm; al–al 34.9 ± 2.1 / 31.4 ± 2.0 mm; zy–zy ≈135–140 / 127–132 mm (Farkas, North American White, direct anthropometry). Only the n–gn and ex–ex SDs are sourced.

queue.claim: Whole-face 3D shape classifies sex at about 90–96% (Mahalanobis D ≈ 3–3.5), and human raters reach about 95% on hair-concealed photos (Bruce et al. 1993). This sets the sex-axis prior sigma at 2/D ≈ 0.65.

queue.claim: The soft-tissue depth difference between the sexes depends on region. Men are about 12–18% thicker at the philtrum, lips and chin (γ = ln(M/F) ≈ +0.10 to +0.18); women are thicker at the lateral orbit, inferior malar area and gonion (γ ≈ −0.05 to −0.10).
